title: Path With Minimum Effort
summary: Walk across a height map from corner to corner so that the steepest single step is as gentle as possible.

tests.explain: Going 1 → 2 → 3 → 6 → 2 has steps of 1, 1, 3 and 4, so its effort is 4. Every route has to make a step of at least 4 somewhere.
You start on the destination, so no step is needed: 0.
Go down the left column and along the bottom row: every cell is 1, so the effort is 0. Crossing the 100s would cost 99.

hints: The cost of a route is not a sum: it is the largest height difference between two consecutive cells on it.
Dijkstra still works if 'distance' means 'effort so far'. Extending a route to a neighbour gives max(effort, |height difference|), which never decreases, just like a sum of non-negative weights.
Pop the cell with the smallest effort from a min-heap. The first time you pop the bottom-right cell, its effort is the answer.

complexity.time: O(R·C · log(R·C)): every cell has 4 neighbours and each heap operation is logarithmic
complexity.space: O(R·C): the best-effort grid and the heap
